dominant_strengths: Hero product photography is impeccably lit and retouched, conveying premium craft and material fidelity at marketing-grade level
Typographic hierarchy uses SF Pro confidently—Apple wordmark lockup with 'Vision Pro' feels iconic and disciplined
Tight adherence to Apple.com global nav system creates instant brand trust and frictionless navigation conventions
dominant_weaknesses: Composition is conservative—centered headshot on white is a recycled Apple template, offering little distinctiveness for a category-defining product
Subhead 'New powerful M5 chip and comfortable Dual Knit Band' is feature-listy and emotionally flat for a spatial computing pitch
Reflective payoff is thin: the page communicates 'expensive headset' but not the worldview or use-case ambition behind Vision Pro
fix_priorities: Rewrite hero copy to evoke spatial experience, not spec-sheet bullets—lead with what the wearer sees, not the chip
Break the centered-on-white pattern with an environmental or POV shot to differentiate from iPhone/Mac hero pages
Introduce subtle motion (parallax lenses, ambient reflection in visor) to hint at the device's dynamic nature on load
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral pull from product photography and behavioral clarity from familiar nav, but reflective meaning underdelivers for a paradigm product.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes—it is unmistakably an Apple Vision Pro product page, executed to house-style standards, though it leans on template rather than reinventing for the category.
